public_rationale: The launch-day record shows impressive but uneven performance. It does not provide a broad human comparison capable of settling the AGI assertion under the ordinary reading specified here. Neither beta status nor isolated errors proves that a system is not AGI. The retrieved evidence therefore does not justify a definitive verdict.
limitations: AGI is undefined in the source.
The available launch-day independent testing was informal and limited.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Grok 3, as demoed, was not AGI, contrary to a Musk fan's prediction.

our_interpretation: The antecedent is the prediction of AGI, rather than the separate promise of being the smartest AI.
The ordinary reading of AGI is general, adaptable competence at approximately human level across a broad range of intellectual tasks. It does not require perfect answers.
The target is the launch version demonstrated on February 17 US time, February 18 UTC.
criteria.support_condition: Evaluations of the launch version establish substantial, systematic limitations inconsistent with broadly general human-level competence.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evaluations establish that the launch version exhibited broadly general human-level competence under the stated reading.

evidence.explanation: Karpathy reported difficult coding successes alongside failures in other tasks and explicitly described his exercise as a short informal test. This establishes uneven capabilities, but does not measure whether the launch model crossed a broad human-level threshold.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A documented evaluation of the launch checkpoint covering generalization and varied intellectual tasks, with human baselines and an explicit AGI criterion.
